To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have designed a new class of Plk1 polo box domain inhibitors, (2) we have identified the key binding interactions of the inhibitors with the Plk1 domain, (3) we have determined the crystal structure of the Plk polo box domain in complex with one of the inhibitors, (4) the inhibitors are selective for the polo box domain, and (5) the inhibitors are cell-permeable and inhibit Plk1 activity in cells.
we have identified a novel class of ligands with low nanomolar binding affinity for the polo-box domain of Plk1 that are based on the N-terminal Pro residue of the PLHSpT pentapeptide.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel peptidic ligands targeting Plk1, a serine-threonine kinase which is overexpressed in many cancers.
the design and synthesis of small molecules that can be used as tools to study the function of Plk1 in the context of cell division and as potential therapeutic agents.
the development of new peptoid-peptide hybrid ligands, and demonstrates the potential for such ligands as a new class of affinity-enhancing scaffolds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
peptoids are useful for the generation of high-affinity ligands for protein targets.
the N-terminal phenyl moiety of the peptoid ligand plays an essential role in Plk1 binding.

peptoid-peptide hybrids are a promising class of molecules for targeting protein-protein interactions, and that this work provides a proof-of-concept for their application in the design of small-molecule inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a class of peptidomimetic ligands with low-nanomole affinity for the Plk1 PBD that are amenable to further optimization.
we have identified peptoids and peptoids-based ligands that bind to the polo box domain and that these ligands are useful for studying the polo box domain.
peptoid-peptide hybrids can be used to create ligands for protein targets with high affinity and high specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peptoid moiety can be used to enhance the affinity of a peptide ligand, without compromising specificity.
the peptoid scaffold can be exploited for affinity enhancement of peptide ligands.
the N-terminal Pro residue in PLHSpT is dispensable for binding to the polo box domain, and can be replaced by peptoid or amide moieties without loss of affinity.
